newsitem.title: USA: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS - Issues to Watch - Sept 18.
newsitem.headline: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS - Issues to Watch - Sept 18.

text.p: -- Allied Waste Industries Inc said it would buy the solid waste management operations of Laidlaw Inc for $1.5 billion in cash, stock and notes.

-- Tambrands Inc said it would take a $46 million pretax charge to close four of its nine manufacturing facilities, cut 17 percent of its workforce, and consolidate its domestic and international groups.
Tambrands closed at 41-3/4 on the NYSE.
-- Chrysler Corp and Canadian auto workers reached tentative agreement on a new labor contract. Chrysler closed up 1/4 to 28-5/8.

-- Published reports quoted court filings in Minnesota's lawsuit against the tobacco industry as saying officials and researchers from tobacco companies may have discussed the need to destroy or hide certain sensitive documents.

-- CFC International Inc said third-quarter earnings will fall below estimates and year-ago levels. It cited a new product, a delayed delivery schedule, and expenses for market research in the Pacific Rim. CFC closed at 16.
-- Citation Corp said after the market close on Tuesday that its fiscal year earnings would fall 15 to 20 percent below forecast levels. Citation closed up 3/16 to 11-7/8.

-- Information Storage Devices Inc said it expects a third quarter loss of $0.30 a share on revenues of around $7.5 million, compared with a profit of $0.19 a share on revenues of $15.5 million in the year-ago quarter.
Information Storage shares fell 1/4 to 6-3/4 on Tuesday, and touched a new low of 6-1/2 during the session.
-- Santa Fe Energy will announce plans to split into two separate companies today, the Wall Street Journal reported. Its shares closed at 13.
